SQL for the cells within d_km of a set of source cells

Source: R/cells_within.R
cells_within_sql.Rd

A cell is within d_km of a source cell when the great-circle (haversine, R = 6371.0088 km) distance between the two CELL CENTRES is at most d_km. For each source cell the candidates are a window of rows (+- ceiling(d / row height) + 1) and columns (the exact longitude reach of a d_km cap at the source latitude, asin(sin(d/R) / cos(lat)); every column when the cap holds a pole), the column index wrapping modulo nc (so a cell at 179.975 E reaches the cells at -179.975) and the rows clipped at the poles; the haversine filter then decides. The grid is cell_id = row * nc + col + 1, row 0 at ymax (90 N), col 0 at xmin (-180), deg per cell – global05 by default (grid_spec_for("global05")), any regular global grid by argument.

Usage

cells_within_sql(src, d_km, by = NULL, nc = 7200L, nr = 3600L, deg = 0.05)

Arguments

src

character; a relation with a cell_id column and, optionally, the grouping column by (e.g. mdl_key): the result is distinct (by, cell_id).

d_km

numeric; the distance, km (> 0).

by

character or NULL; the grouping column of src carried through.

nc, nr

integer; the grid's columns and rows (7200 x 3600).

deg

numeric; the cell size in degrees (0.05). nc * deg must be 360 and nr * deg 180.

Value

SQL selecting distinct [by,] cell_id (INTEGER).

Details

Land cells are included (the whole-range convention); the caller masks if it wants to.

Examples

cat(cells_within_sql("src_cells", 100))
#> WITH s AS (
#>   SELECT cell_id,
#>          (CAST(cell_id AS BIGINT) - 1) // 7200 AS r0, (CAST(cell_id AS BIGINT) - 1) % 7200 AS c0,
#>          90 - ((CAST(cell_id AS BIGINT) - 1) // 7200 + 0.5) * 0.05   AS lat0,
#>          -180 + ((CAST(cell_id AS BIGINT) - 1) % 7200 + 0.5) * 0.05  AS lon0
#>   FROM src_cells),
#> w AS (
#>   SELECT *, CASE WHEN sin(100 / 6371.0088) / cos(radians(lat0)) >= 1 THEN 7200
#>                  ELSE CAST(ceil(degrees(asin(sin(100 / 6371.0088) / cos(radians(lat0)))) / 0.05) AS INTEGER) + 1 END AS dcm
#>   FROM s),
#> cand AS (
#>   SELECT lat0, lon0, r0 + dr AS r1, ((c0 + dc) % 7200 + 7200) % 7200 AS c1
#>   FROM w, range(-19, 19 + 1) a(dr),
#>           generate_series(-least(dcm, 3600), least(dcm, 3600)) b(dc)
#>   WHERE r0 + dr BETWEEN 0 AND 3599),
#> cand2 AS (
#>   SELECT lat0, lon0, r1, c1,
#>          90 - (r1 + 0.5) * 0.05 AS lat1, -180 + (c1 + 0.5) * 0.05 AS lon1
#>   FROM cand)
#> SELECT DISTINCT CAST(r1 * 7200 + c1 + 1 AS INTEGER) AS cell_id
#> FROM cand2
#> WHERE 2 * 6371.0088 * asin(sqrt(least(1,
#>         pow(sin(radians(lat1 - lat0) / 2), 2) +
#>         cos(radians(lat0)) * cos(radians(lat1)) * pow(sin(radians(lon1 - lon0) / 2), 2)))) <= 100
